title: Prefill-aware kernel budgeting and tail smoothing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Under mixed workloads (short chat queries + long prefill-heavy requests) our continuous batching runtime occasionally forms very large decode batches that degrade 95/99 latency for interactive tenants. Root causes: naive kernel selection that optimistically packs long KV caches with low-precedence decode work, and admission logic that doesn't account for per-request prefill cost or attention stride differences. Goal: implement a prefill-aware kernel budgeting layer and tail-smoothing admission policy that jointly optimize kernel choice, per-batch token budget, and probabilistic hold for tail requests to reduce 99th percentile latency without significant throughput loss. Expected outcomes: 20-40% reduction in p99 for interactive routes under mixed load, <=10% throughput regression on heavy prefill workloads, measurable unit-cost neutrality via dynamic kernel downselection for large prefill items.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency improvement >= 20% on interactive route in synthetic mixed workload (50% short/50% long) compared to baseline
Throughput on dedicated GPU pool drops by <= 10% in worst-case synthetic prefill-heavy test
No regressions on model output correctness or KV-cache integrity (unit tests + end-to-end smoke)
Canary rollout plan documented and automated via rollout API; rollback on >5% error rate or >30% latency increase
Observability: new per-batch kernel_budget and prefill_cost metrics emitted; dashboards and alerts created
tasks: Design: kernel budget model that estimates per-request kernel-cost based on sequence-length distribution and attention stride
Implement: admission controller extension to compute per-request prefill_weight and assign token_budget per batch
Implement: kernel downselection policies that prefer quantized kernels when budget > threshold and latency-SLO is relaxed
Implement: probabilistic tail-smoothing hold (configurable lambda) to spread tail arrivals across micro-windows
Add unit/integration tests for KV-cache correctness under re-ordered prefill/decode execution
Add telemetry: emit kernel_budget, prefill_weight, batch_hold_ms, batch_composition tags per batch
Benchmark: run mixed-load perf harness and collect p50/p95/p99 and throughput/cost metrics
Docs: PRD update and operational runbook for rollback and tuning knobs
Canary: orchestrate staged rollout to 5% traffic then 30% then global with automated health checks
